title: Hattie the Mouse and the Lego Airplane
summary: When young Izzy the Kiddo finds herself stuck in bed with a cold, her friend Hattie the Mouse pays a visit to cheer her up. Rejecting soup in favor of creativity, the pair dives into a world of building blocks. Joined by a Lego architect named Uncle Bill, they construct elaborate symmetrical stairs and a soaring airplane, proving that a little imagination is the best medicine for any illness.

highlightQuote.text: Hattie, be very quiet. I'm sick and I'm resting, so you better be very, very, very quiet.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Once upon a time...

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Hattie, be very quiet. I'm sick and I'm resting, so you better be very, very, very quiet.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Once upon a time, Izzy the kiddo was sick and she was resting, and Hattie the Mouse came to visit her. Hattie the mouse said, 'Oh hello Izzy, I heard you're sick. How are you feeling?'

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: I'm good, but I'm a little sick. So I'm resting in bed and I'm going... Achoo! Achoo! I'm sick.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: And Hattie said 'Gesundheit! Here's a tissue.' And Hattie said, 'Is there anything I can bring you? Would you like, um, some soup?'

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: No, I just need to play with some Legos.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Oh some Legos! I'll bring you some Legos. And so Hattie went to her house and got a big box of Legos and she brought them to Izzy the Kiddo. 'Izzy!'

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: And Izzy said, 'I already have some Legos which I can build with.'

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Oh. And Hattie the Mouse said, 'Can I play Legos with you, Izzy?'

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Of course. What should we build together?

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: What should we build?

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Well, first I have to go build with Uncle Bill, Uncle Bill, Uncle, Uncle, Uncle Bill. Uncle... Uncle Bill. Daddy can you help me find Uncle Bill?

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Yeah. Oh, I see him, he's right here.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Uncle Bill, what do you work on today?

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Oh, well, I'm working on building something very special.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: But I'm going to build with Legos too.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Oh you are? I'm going to build some stairs.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: I'm building stairs too.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Little brick.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: And so, even though Izzy the Kiddo was feeling sick, she had a good time building with Legos with her friend Hattie the Mouse. And what did they build together? What did they make?

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: And Uncle Bill says, 'Aha! Here's my thing that I made. What do you think of that?'

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: I like it, Uncle Bill.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Thank you. It's symmetrical. It's got stairs on both sides.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Uncle Bill, look what I'm making. I made a little airplane for you.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Wow! What a cool airplane. Thanks for making that, Izzy. And what did Hattie the Mouse build?

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Hattie-ma, look at your airplane, for you and Uncle Bill. Wow what a cool airplane.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Izzy, can you make it fly?

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Wait, I'll attach the bottom. See how it flies and flies way up high into the sky.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Wow, it's flying high up in the sky. Oh, and that's our timer. So that's the end of Stars and Stories and Lego School. And Hattie the Mouse said, 'Bye bye, Izzy, I hope you feel better.' And that's the end.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Okay, let's tuck in our Legos again.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Why?

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Cause it's time for your nap.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Well, I'll tuck in my airplane.

characters.name: Isabella
characters.description: A towering Dimitar scholar and alchemist of Atsukeeseet, Mama Izzy is a clever kiddo at heart and a steadfast guardian of rooftop gardens and intricate dollhouses. Gifted with the power of flight, she navigates the open heights with aquatic grace, her massive frame often shielded by a special protective metal that glimmers even as she descends into the shadows. As a resourceful quartermaster, she employs red flashlights, gold-laced slimes, and pipe cleaners to mend a Lanternshark’s failing light, yet her generosity remains her hallmark; she freely shares her vast library, brokers homes for dragons, and teaches others to find the resonance in their own voices. Her most profound magic resides in her vast, soft blanket—a sanctuary of ultimate coziness—where she remains a brave, quick-witted protector to all who honor her singular request for absolute silence.

characters.name: Hattie the Mouse
characters.description: A nimble, friendly mouse of Possible Street and loyal friend to Izzy and Seeker, this brave artisan is the wife of Dimitar and mistress of the Workshop of Hats—a weathered hollow tree sanctuary on Cornell Street scented with cedar, ink, and peanut butter toast. Clad in her signature red cloak and pointy hat, she is a resourceful hatmaker whose spirit was forged against massive diggers and the rain-slicked Floofer Cloud. Within her paint-stained home, she carefully curates her husband’s library alongside her own hand-painted volumes while confronting a baffling supply mystery; the discovery of curious clover stickers signals a gathering shadow of intrigue she is determined to unravel.

characters.name: Uncle Bill
characters.description: A diligent crew member and master Lego architect, this former visitor to Balloon World crafts perfectly symmetrical stairways and shapes iridescent purple slime into glistening rocket ships. Renowned for a sharp eye that once pierced Pluto’s crystalline shadows, they recently turned their gaze toward the forest’s depths, acting as a compassionate friend to discover and tend to a sick creature hidden in the brush. Whether providing blocks for builders, weaving bedtime stories, or offering woodland mercy, they remain a helpful soul. Yet, between these moments of structural precision and quiet rescue, they harbor a penchant for deep rest, often found napping peacefully inside the colorful confines of a toy container, tucked away amidst the playthings they share.
